results.title: Neocloud vs hyperscaler GPU: what capacity costs | Casitel
highlights:
Neocloud vs hyperscaler GPU rates for the H100, H200 and B200, read on 3 November 2026, with published commitment discounts and what else changes the bill.

C Compute · H100 list rates, per GPU-hour Rates read 3 November 2026

$3.99 lowest H100 rate in this note, at Lambda and E2E Networks

Each provider's own page, read 3 November 2026. Not executed prices.

...

The other side is the hyperscalers: Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle. They sell GPUs as one product inside a much larger cloud.

## What the rate cards say

All rates below are US dollars per GPU-hour, taken from each provider's own page on 3 November 2026. They are list rates. They are not what large buyers sign.

Provider H100 H200 B200 What the rate is

Lambda$3.99 Not listed$6.69 On-demand, 8-GPU instance

E2E Networks$3.99$5.29$7.99 On-demand

Nebius$4.50$5.40$8.50 On-demand, HGX

CoreWeave$6.16$6.31$8.60 On-demand, North America

AWS$5.97$6.87$14.21 Capacity Blocks, a short reservation

Google Cloud$9.80$10.71 Not read Vertex AI, managed service

Oracle$10.00$10.00$14.00 Pay as you go

Microsoft Azure$12.29 Not read Not read ND H100 v5, East US

Three of these need a note. CoreWeave and Azure price a whole 8-GPU machine by the hour: $49.24 and $98.32 for the H100. The per-GPU figures above are our own arithmetic. AWS publishes a plain on-demand rate only in its calculator, so the AWS row is its Capacity Blocks price, and for the H200 it is the p5e machine (the p5en costs $7.90). Google's row is the Vertex AI managed service, which is not the same product as a bare virtual machine.

Even so, the spread is wide. The H100 runs from $3.99 to $12.29, about three times. The B200 runs from $6.69 to $14.21, about twice. Rate cards also move. In our read on 8 October, Nebius showed $3.85 for an H100. On 3 November it showed $4.50.

## What commitments change

Every provider here says a commitment lowers the rate. Few publish by how much.

C Compute · published commitment discounts Read 3 Nov 2026

E2E Networks 10% to 30%, its own figure

Sakura Internet 5% for 6 months, 10% for 12

Each provider's own pages, read 3 Nov 2026. Discounts off list rates.

- CoreWeave says it offers up to 60% off its on-demand prices for committed use. That is its own claim. The page lists no committed rate.
- Azure publishes reservation prices through its public price API. For the H100 machine in East US, the one-year price works out 36% below pay as you go and the three-year price 56% below. We divided each term price by its hours.
- Google Cloud lists Flexible Savings Plan rates on the Vertex AI page. For the H200 they are $9.64 for one year and $8.57 for three, which is 10% and 20% below $10.71.
- E2E Networks says three-month, six-month and annual commitments can earn 10% to 30%, depending on length and volume.
- Sakura Internet announced on 1 July 2026 a commitment plan for one H100 plan: 5% off for six months and 10% off for twelve.
- AWS cut P5 (H100) prices by 44% for on-demand and 45% for the three-year Instance Savings Plan from 1 June 2025. Those are cuts from its earlier prices, not discounts off today's rate.
- Nebius and Lambda name no percentage. Both point large buyers to sales.

results.title: GPU rental prices in 2026: H100, H200 and B200 per hour
results.author: Safeguard Security Team
highlights:
In October 2026, published on-demand list prices for an H100 ranged from about $2 to about $12 per GPU-hour, depending on the provider, the billing model and what is bundled. Specialist clouds mostly sit between $3 and $6. Spot and long commitments can cut the price by half or more. B200 list prices run from about $6 to $14.

...

- AWS Capacity Blocks, p5.48xlarge (8 H100s), N. Virginia, Ohio and Oregon: $47.757 per instance-hour, $5.970 per GPU-hour. AWS Capacity Blocks pricing page, 19 October 2026.
- AWS p5.48xlarge on-demand (8 H100s), N. Virginia, Ohio, Oregon: $6.88 per GPU-hour, as checked by IntuitionLabs on 10 October 2026.
- Azure NC40ads H100 v5 (1 GPU), East US, Linux pay-as-you-go: $6.98 per hour. Azure ND96isr H100 v5 (8 GPUs): $98.32 per VM-hour, $12.29 per GPU-hour. Azure Retail Prices API, 19 October 2026.
- Google Cloud a3-highgpu-8g (8 H100s), Iowa, on-demand: $88.49 per VM-hour, which is $11.06 per GPU-hour. IntuitionLabs, 10 October 2026.
- Oracle Cloud BM.GPU.H100.8: $10.00 per GPU-hour list. IntuitionLabs, 10 October 2026.
- CoreWeave HGX H100, 8 GPUs, on-demand: $49.24 per instance-hour, about $6.16 per GPU. CoreWeave pricing page, 19 October 2026.
- Lambda H100 SXM, 8-GPU instance: $3.99 per GPU-hour. Lambda pricing page, 19 October 2026. IntuitionLabs records $2.99 in a 2025 snapshot.
- Runpod H100 SXM: $3.99 Secure Cloud and $2.69 Community Cloud. H100 PCIe: $1.99 Community Cloud. Runpod pricing page, 19 October 2026.
- Nebius HGX H100 on demand: $4.50 per GPU-hour. Nebius prices page, 19 October 2026. IntuitionLabs says this took effect on 1 October 2026, up from $3.85.
- H200 on-demand list prices: $5.29 (Runpod Secure Cloud), $5.40 (Nebius), about $6.31 (CoreWeave, $50.44 per 8-GPU instance). Provider pages, 19 October 2026.
- B200 on-demand list prices: $6.69 (Lambda, 8 GPUs), $7.99 (Runpod Secure Cloud), $8.50 (Nebius), $8.60 (CoreWeave, $68.80 per 8-GPU instance). AWS Capacity Blocks: $14.208. Provider pages, 19 October 2026.
- B200 index price: $2.31 per hour in early March 2026 and $4.95 in late April 2026, per the Ornn Compute Price Index as reported on tomtunguz.com on 27 April 2026.

...

A GPU-hour is one GPU rented for one

...

The IntuitionLabs survey says plainly that its entries mix prepaid capacity, on-demand VMs, pods, and cluster and node rates, and are not interchangeable. Its inclusion rule is publicly displayed hourly rates for a matching product, taken from first-party pages, with promotional rates excluded. It is a survey by one publisher, not an official price index, and its method is as the publisher describes it.

## H100: the 2026 snapshot

The H100 is the older workhorse. Here is the picture from the 10 October 2026 survey and provider pages read on 19 October 2026.

The large clouds charge the most on-demand. IntuitionLabs lists AWS at $6.88 per GPU-hour for the 8-GPU instance in three US regions and $8.60 in N. California. Azure's own price feed shows $6.98 for a single-GPU VM and $98.32 for the 8-GPU VM in East US, which is $12.29 per GPU. IntuitionLabs lists Google at $11.06 per GPU in Iowa and Oracle at $10.00.

Specialist clouds list lower. Lambda's pricing page shows the 8-GPU H100 SXM at $3.99 per GPU, with smaller instances at $4.09, $4.19 and $4.29 for 4, 2 and 1 GPUs. Runpod's page shows its SXM pod at $3.99 in Secure Cloud and $2.69 in Community Cloud. Lambda's 1-Click Cluster product lists H100 at $6.16 per GPU for 16 GPUs, $5.85 for 64 and $5.54 for 256, for terms of two weeks to a year. CoreWeave's on-demand HGX H100 instance works out at about $6.16 per GPU. IntuitionLabs also reports one marketplace query on 10 October that returned single-GPU H100 SXM offers from about $1.68 per hour on an unverified host, and is clear that a marketplace query is not a list price.

Several of these went up. According to the survey, AWS Capacity Blocks rose from $5.19 to $5.97, Runpod Secure Cloud H100 SXM from $3.29 to $3.99, Lambda's 8-GPU SXM from $2.99 (a 2025 snapshot) to $3.99, and Nebius's HGX H100 from $3.85 to $4.50 effective 1 October 2026. The current figures match the providers' own pages on 19 October 2026. The survey says AWS on-demand and Azure list prices were not re-verified as lower than the 2025 third-party figures.

...

## H200 and B200

The H200 is a later Hopper chip with more and faster memory, about 141 GB of HBM3e per GPU on AWS's P5e and P5en instances. The B200 is NVIDIA's Blackwell generation GPU; Lambda's page lists it with 180 GB of memory.

First-party list prices on 19 October 2026 give a clearer picture than earlier in the year:

- H200 on-demand: Runpod Secure Cloud $5.29 and Community Cloud $3.59; Nebius $5.40; CoreWeave $50.44 per 8-GPU instance, about $6.31 per GPU.
- H200 Capacity Blocks on AWS: $6.866 per GPU-hour on p5e.48xlarge and $7.895 on p5en.48xlarge, in the US regions listed.
- B200 on-demand: Lambda $6.69 per GPU on an 8-GPU instance and $6.99 for one GPU; Runpod Secure Cloud $7.99 and Community Cloud $5.98; Nebius $8.50; CoreWeave $68.80 per 8-GPU instance, about $8.60 per GPU.
- B200 Capacity Blocks on AWS: $113.666 per instance-hour, $14.208 per GPU-hour, on p6-b200.48xlarge.
- B200 clusters on Lambda: $9.86 per GPU for 16 GPUs, $9.36 for 64 and $8.87 for 256 or more, for terms of two weeks to a year.

AWS's Capacity Blocks page says its rates are updated regularly, with the next update scheduled for January 2027, and that a block is charged at the rate in effect when it is bought.

The index view is different. The Ornn Compute Price Index, reported in a post dated 27 April 2026 on tomtunguz.com, put the B200 at $4.95 per hour that week, up from $2.31 in early March, a 114% rise in six weeks. The author also reports that the B200 premium over H200 fell to $0.28 per hour in November 2025 and widened to $1.80 by late April 2026. That is one index, from one author, describing a spot style market, so its levels sit below most on-demand list prices. The takeaway is directional: Blackwell prices were rising in spring 2026, and the gap to the previous generation was widening.

...

List prices are the starting point of a negotiation for large buyers. The IntuitionLabs survey says Oracle's price, for example, is a pay-as-you-go list price in US dollars before negotiated discounts. Lambda's page asks buyers of clusters for a year or longer to contact sales, and Nebius lists GB200 and GB300 NVL72 systems as contact sales. A company buying thousands of GPUs on a multi-year contract will not pay list. Those deals are private and are not reported in public price lists or the surveys cited here.

...

Firm: the list prices shown on the AWS Capacity Blocks, CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius and Runpod pricing pages and in the Azure Retail Prices API on 19 October 2026. Also firm, as a dated survey: the IntuitionLabs figures checked on 10 October 2026 from first-party pages, including the AWS on-demand, Google and Oracle prices not confirmed here directly. Also firm as reports: the Ornn index figures as quoted on tomtunguz.com.

results.title: What an H100 hour lists for at Azure and Oracle, next to the rental marketplaces (with the VM named) - Show and Tell - Hugging Face Forums
highlights:
“From $X per GPU-hour” is the number everyone quotes for the big clouds, usually without saying which machine you have to rent to get it. I added two clouds whose price lists can be read without an account — Azure and Oracle Cloud — to the rental prices we already collect hourly, and kept the machine attached to every number.

One reading, 2 Oct 2026, 13:00 UTC, USD per GPU-hour:

| GPU | Vast.ai median (offers) | RunPod from | Azure from | Oracle Cloud from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A100 | 0.74 (58) | 1.39 | 3.40 — ND96asr v4, 8 × 40 GB, VM 27.20/h | 3.05 — BM.GPU4.8, 8 × 40 GB, machine 24.40/h |
| H100 | 2.27 (8) | 2.69 | 6.98 — NC40ads H100 v5, 1 × 94 GB | 10.00 — BM.GPU.H100.8, 8 × 80 GB, machine 80.00/h |
| H200 | 5.12 (7) | 3.59 | 10.60 — ND96isr H200 v5, 8 × 141 GB, VM 84.80/h | 10.00 — BM.GPU.H200.8, 8 × 141 GB, machine 80.00/h |
| B200 | 7.81 (6) | 5.98 | not listed as its own size | 14.00 — BM.GPU.B200.8, 8 × 180 GB, machine 112.00/h |

Three things the table shows at this reading:

1. The per-GPU price hides the unit of sale. Azure’s H100 at 6.98 is a one-card VM you can take alone. Oracle’s 10.00 exists only as an eight-card bare-metal machine at 80.00 an hour. For the A100 both clouds’ lowest per-GPU price sits in an eight-card machine with the 40 GB card; a single 80 GB A100 on Azure lists at 3.67.
2. The gap to the marketplace is larger on the two older cards. List price against the Vast.ai median of the same hour: A100 4.6× (Azure) and 4.1× (Oracle), H100 3.1× and 4.4×; H200 about 2× for both, B200 1.8× (Oracle). One reading, and the marketplace side is thin for the newer classes (six to eight offers) — a description of today, not a trend.
3. The two clouds do not rank the same way per class. Oracle is below Azure on the A100 and the H200, above it on the H100.

What it does not say: availability (a list price is not free capacity), what you pay with a commitment or a negotiated rate, or that a cloud VM and a marketplace host are the same product — they are not; the table compares prices, nothing else.

How the numbers are made: Azure publishes whole-VM prices per region, so the per-GPU price is the Linux pay-as-you-go price divided by the GPU count from Microsoft’s size documentation, lowest across documented sizes and public regions; sizes the price list carries but the documentation does not describe are left out rather than guessed. Oracle prices a GPU-hour directly and has one list without regions. Both are read four times a day and shown beside the marketplace medians, never blended into them.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Index, November 2026: H100 to B300
highlights:
Every month we check the public on-demand prices of specialist GPU clouds to set our own: CoreGPU prices every GPU at least 25% below the market median. This is the data behind that number, as listed on November 4, 2026.

## Method

- One on-demand price per provider and GPU, taken from public pricing pages or price APIs. Prices for 8-GPU nodes are divided by eight.
- Specialist GPU clouds only for the median. Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle) are listed separately because their prices are 2.5 to 4.5 times higher.
- Monthly cost = hourly price × 730 hours. Prices exclude taxes.

## Median prices by GPU

| GPU | Prices found | Lowest $/h | Median $/h | Median / month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA B300 | 8 | 6.60 | 8.98 | $6,552 |
| NVIDIA B200 | 11 | 5.43 | 8.19 | $5,979 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 12 | 2.90 | 4.94 | $3,606 |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | 16 | 1.99 | 3.72 | $2,716 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 9 | 1.40 | 2.19 | $1,599 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 11 | 0.73 | 1.57 | $1,146 |
| AMD MI325X | 2 | 3.80 | 4.21 | $3,071 |
| AMD MI300X | 4 | 2.59 | 3.22 | $2,351 |

...

## Hyperscalers

On-demand prices per GPU-hour at the largest clouds remain far above specialist clouds: H100 from $6.88 (8-GPU instance divided by eight) to more than $12 depending on the provider, and B300 from $15 to $17.80. Commitments of one to three years cut those prices by 30 to 56%.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.

results.title: Cloud GPU Pricing 2026: H100, B200 and RTX Rental Costs
results.author: Boris Sedu
highlights:
- An H100 costs about $2–12 per GPU-hour on demand depending on the provider: around $2 on marketplaces, $4–6 on AI-focused clouds such as Lambda, RunPod, Nebius and CoreWeave, and $7–12 on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and Oracle.
- Newer GPUs cost more per hour but not always per job. A B200 rents for about $6.70–8.50 on AI clouds, but it trains roughly twice as fast as an H100, so the total cost of a job can be the same or lower.
- Consumer and mid-range GPUs are cheap: an RTX 4090 or RTX 5090 rents for roughly $0.30–1.20 per hour, an A100 80GB for $0.70–3.50.
- Prices rose in 2026. Nebius raised on-demand prices by about 17–21% on October 1, AWS raised Capacity Block prices three times, and several clouds moved the H100 from $2.99 to $3.99 per hour.
- Newer GPUs and better software change the math. In MLPerf Training 2026, NVIDIA’s GB300 was 1.3–1.6 times faster than the GB200, and the independent ClusterMAX rating put CoreWeave and Nebius at the top for cluster quality.
- Spot and reserved capacity cut costs by roughly 30–80%, but spot instances can be interrupted at any moment, and reservations lock you in.

...

| GPU | Memory | Typical price per GPU-hour | Examples (on-demand) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA RTX 4090 | 24 GB | $0.30–0.90 | Vast.ai from about $0.30; RunPod $0.89 |
| NVIDIA RTX 5090 | 32 GB | $0.50–1.20 | Vast.ai from about $0.50; RunPod $1.19 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 48 GB | $0.90–1.90 | RunPod $1.09; Nebius from $1.55; AWS g6e.xlarge $1.86 |
| NVIDIA A100 | 80 GB | $0.70–3.50 | marketplaces under $1; RunPod $1.79; Lambda $2.79; AWS p4de $3.43 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 96 GB | $2–3 | RunPod $2.49 |
| NVIDIA H100 | 80 GB | $2–12.30 | Vast.ai $2.14; Lambda $3.99; RunPod $3.99 (SXM); Nebius $4.50; AWS $6.88; Google Cloud $11.06; Azure $12.29 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 141 GB | $5–8 | RunPod $5.29; Nebius $5.40; AWS p5en about $7.91 |
| NVIDIA B200 | 180 GB | $6.70–14.30 | Lambda $6.69; RunPod $7.99; Nebius $8.50; AWS p6-b200 $14.24 |
| NVIDIA B300 | 288 GB | $9–18 | RunPod $8.99; Nebius $9.50; AWS p6-b300 $17.80 |

...

- Hyperscalers: AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud. The most expensive per GPU-hour, but they offer everything around the GPU: managed Kubernetes, storage, databases, networking, security and compliance certifications, and enterprise support. They make sense if your data and the rest of your infrastructure are already there, or if you have credits or negotiated discounts. Getting large H100 or B200 quotas often requires a request to support or a reservation.
- AI-focused clouds (neoclouds): CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius, Crusoe, RunPod, Together AI, Hyperbolic and others. They specialize in GPUs, typically charge half as much as hyperscalers or less, and offer clusters with fast InfiniBand interconnect for multi-node training. Fewer surrounding services, but for training and inference that is often all you need.
- GPU marketplaces and community clouds: Vast.ai, RunPod Community Cloud. Independent hosts and data centers rent out their GPUs, including consumer cards like the RTX 4090 and 5090. The cheapest option, but reliability, network speed and security vary from host to host, so they suit experiments and jobs that can survive interruptions better than sensitive data.
- Notebooks with free and cheap GPUs: Google Colab, Kaggle. Colab’s free tier gives limited, unguaranteed access to a GPU for sessions of up to 12 hours; Colab Pro costs $9.99 per month for 100 compute units, which buys roughly 80 hours on a T4 or 13 hours on an A100 80GB. Kaggle notebooks offer free GPU sessions of up to 12 hours with a weekly quota, commonly reported at around 30 hours. Ideal for learning, not for long training runs.

...

- Nebius raised on-demand prices on October 1, 2026: H100 from $3.85 to $4.50 per hour, H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- AWS raised prices of EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML, its reserved GPU capacity, by about 15% in January 2026, by about 20% in July (P5 with H100 to $5.19 per GPU-hour, P6-B200 to $12.36) and again in October.
- RunPod and Lambda list the H100 SXM at $3.99 per hour; in spring 2026 both were quoted at $2.99 or less. RunPod’s B200 rose from about $5.89 to $7.99.

results.author: Paul Nugent
highlights:
AWS is raising GPU instance prices by ~20% on July 1 — and quietly keeping its own Trainium chips at the same price.

This is the most important AI infrastructure pricing story of the year, and the signal is unmistakable.

The move: ~20% price increase on EC2 Capacity Block reservations for Nvidia GPU instances, effective July 1. AWS cited "supply and demand dynamics" — meaning the global compute crunch has gotten severe enough that AWS believes customers will pay more without leaving.

results.title: Four pricing changes in eight days at one provider. None at another. | Compute Stacker
results.author: Compute Stacker
highlights:
Four pricing changes in eight days at one provider. None at another.

What actually happened on H100 rate cards this month:

- October 1: Nebius raised on-demand H100 from $3.85 to $4.50, up 16.9%, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50, up 21%. Its second increase in three months.
- October 7: AWS reserved Capacity Blocks moved to $5.970 per H100 accelerator-hour, the same rate across twelve regions.
- October 8: Nebius switched preemptible H100, H200, B200, B300 and RTX PRO 6000 to dynamic spot pricing. The published $2.15 became a floor of $0.79, with prices that can change every 15 minutes, including during a run, capped one cent below the on-demand rate.
- CoreWeave's HGX H100 node stayed at $49.24, or $6.16 per GPU.

...

1. Per GPU or per node. CoreWeave, Oracle, Google and Azure sell H100s as 8-GPU nodes. If you need three, you pay for eight.
2. Volume rules. AWS charges $5.970 whether you take one GPU or eight. Lambda charges $4.29 for one and $3.99 each for eight.
3. Region. Nebius's H100 is in eu-north1 only. Google's 8-GPU H100 varies about 30% between its cheapest and priciest regions.
4. Purchase type. On-demand, spot, reserved and committed can differ by more than 3x on the same chip, with completely different reliability.
5. What's bundled. Lambda and CoreWeave list free egress. AWS charges about $0.09 per GB after an allowance.

results.title: If you picked your H100 provider on price, the answer changed, and nobody lowered a rate to make it change. | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
If you picked your H100 provider on price, the answer changed, and nobody lowered a rate to make it change.

Crusoe’s published H100 read $3.90 in our October 11 catalog and $4.50 in our October 18 catalog. Lambda’s read $3.99 in both. So the lowest published H100 across the nine providers we track rose to $3.99, and the company that now sets it never touched its price.

Crusoe was the only one of those nine whose published price differed between the two catalogs. Its H200 moved the same way, $4.29 to $5.40 across the same two.

Underneath that, the Ornn Compute Price Index, a third-party index of traded prices rather than quoted or listed ones, rose in all four families between its October 11 and October 19 readings. B200 is the clearest case. No provider published anything, and the distance between the lowest published B200 across those nine and the index still more than doubled, from $0.76 on October 11 to $1.72 against the October 19 reading.

One pricing page changed. The market moved on all four.
